methods.label: Find a perpendicular base and height
methods.explanation:
To use \(BC\) as the base, first check whether \(BK\) is perpendicular to it. The interior angles of a hexagon sum to \((6-2)180^\circ=720^\circ\). Since the hexagon is equiangular, each interior angle is \(120^\circ\).

The square gives \(\angle ABJ=90^\circ\), and the equilateral triangle gives \(\angle JBK=60^\circ\). Using the order of the rays shown around \(B\), the remaining angle is
\[
\angle KBC=360^\circ-120^\circ-90^\circ-60^\circ=90^\circ.
\]
Thus \(BK\) is a height for base \(BC\).

The square of area \(18\) has side length \(3\sqrt2\), so \(BK=BJ=AB=3\sqrt2\). Similarly, the square of area \(32\) has side length \(4\sqrt2\), and the given equality yields \(BC=FE=4\sqrt2\). Therefore,
\[
[\triangle KBC]=\frac12(3\sqrt2)(4\sqrt2)=12.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{12}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
